questions.question: Wheelchair seat width should be about:

options.D: The patient's hip width plus about 2 inches

questions.explanation: Too narrow causes pressure; too wide impairs propulsion.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Wheelchair seat depth is measured from the posterior buttock to the popliteal fold, and then:
questions.explanation: Prevents pressure behind the knee.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Footrests should be positioned so the thighs are:

options.D: Supported and the feet clear of the floor by about 2 inches

questions.explanation: Avoid excessive pressure on the ischia.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The backrest height for an active paraplegic user is usually:

options.C: Low (below the inferior scapular angle) to allow trunk movement

questions.explanation: Higher backs for patients with poor trunk control.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Desk-length removable armrests are useful for a wheelchair user to:

options.D: Get closer to tables and make lateral transfers

questions.explanation: Removable armrests aid sliding board transfers.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Hand rims with vertical projections are useful for patients with:
questions.explanation: Projections aid propulsion using the palms.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Anti-tip devices on a wheelchair:
questions.explanation: Removed when performing wheelies.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The recommended maximum slope for a wheelchair ramp is:

options.B: 1:12 (1 inch of rise per 12 inches of ramp)

questions.explanation: A ramp rising 18 inches needs at least 18 feet.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A ramp that rises 18 inches should be at least:
questions.explanation: Using the 1:12 ratio.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The minimum door width for wheelchair access is about:
questions.explanation: A turning space of 60 inches is needed.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: When a therapist assists a patient in a wheelchair to descend a curb, the safest method is to:

options.C: Descend backwards with the therapist in control (large rear wheels first)

questions.explanation: Forward descent risks forward fall.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A wheelchair with a reclining back should have:

options.A: Elevating leg rests to prevent hamstring stretch and pressure

questions.explanation: Reclining shifts weight and improves pressure relief.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which patient would most likely need a power wheelchair?
questions.explanation: Sip-and-puff or chin controls may be used.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Transferring a stroke patient toward the stronger side is usually preferred because:

options.C: The stronger limbs can bear weight and control the movement

questions.explanation: As function improves, practise toward the affected side.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A mechanical (Hoyer) lift is used for:

options.A: Dependent patients who cannot bear weight

questions.explanation: Reduces caregiver injury.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A gait (transfer) belt is applied around the patient's:
questions.explanation: Provides a secure grip.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A depression transfer in C7–C8 tetraplegia relies on strength of:

options.D: Triceps, latissimus dorsi and pectoralis (shoulder depressors)

questions.explanation: Lifts the body between the arms.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Positioning in bed for a patient with hemiplegia emphasises:

options.B: Lying flat on the affected side without support
options.D: Shoulder protraction and hip alignment, avoiding prolonged supine lying with extensor pattern

questions.explanation: Lying on the affected side with the arm forward is encouraged.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Which home modification best reduces fall risk in the bathroom?
questions.explanation: Raised toilet seats also help.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Handrails on stairs should be installed on:
questions.explanation: Contrasting step edges improve visibility.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In planning a kitchen for a wheelchair user, work surfaces should be at a height of about:
questions.explanation: Reachable shelves 15–48 inches.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A lever-type door handle is easier than a knob for patients with:

options.C: Weak grip such as arthritis or stroke

questions.explanation: Universal design.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The comfortable forward reach range of a seated wheelchair user is about:
questions.explanation: Used to plan light switches and shelves.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Environmental control units are used by people with high-level tetraplegia to:

options.C: Operate lights, TV, doors and phones with minimal movement

questions.explanation: Controlled by switches, voice or sip-and-puff.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A resting hand splint after stroke maintains:

options.A: Wrist and finger extension to prevent flexor contracture

questions.explanation: Positioning in a neutral position.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A universal cuff allows a patient with weak grip to:

options.D: Hold utensils such as a spoon or toothbrush

questions.explanation: Used in C6 tetraplegia.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A long opponens splint with a utensil holder is typically used for patients at:
questions.explanation: Positions the thumb for tenodesis grasp.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A four-wheeled rollator with a seat is useful for patients who:

options.C: Tire easily and need rests during walking, such as COPD

questions.explanation: Brakes must be used when sitting.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The correct height of a walking stick is such that the handle is level with the:
questions.explanation: Or the wrist crease with the arm hanging.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A quad cane is preferred over a single-point cane when:

options.B: More stability is needed, such as in hemiplegia

questions.explanation: Wider base of support.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Axillary crutches should be fitted so that there are about:

options.C: 2–3 finger-widths between the axilla and the crutch pad

questions.explanation: Prevents pressure on the brachial plexus.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The first functional skill usually taught after a thoracic SCI is:
questions.explanation: Sequence: bed mobility, sitting balance, transfers, wheelchair skills.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A requirement for functional long sitting in SCI is adequate:

options.A: Hamstring length (straight leg raise about 110–120°) without losing back support

questions.explanation: Do not overstretch the lumbar extensors in tetraplegia.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In a patient with C6–C7 tetraplegia, the hamstrings are stretched fully while the lumbar extensors are:

options.D: Left slightly tight to provide stability for sitting

questions.explanation: Allows the patient to lean on tight back extensors.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A patient with a complete L3 lesion with good quadriceps can ambulate with:

options.B: Bilateral KAFOs or AFOs and forearm crutches

questions.explanation: Quadriceps allow knee control; ankle control via AFO.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Sullivan's Physical Rehabilitation (wheelchair, transfers and assistive technology chapters) (chapter-level reference)
